risks: Low: staff may disclose unsafe practice or criticise colleagues; small sites make roles identifiable.
consent: Written informed consent for interviews; verbal agreement from staff on observed shifts, with the option to be left out of notes; no patient data are recorded during observation.
data: Recordings deleted after summaries are checked; quotations attributed only by profession group, never by site and role together; data held on the network's secure drive.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients arriving at night and at the smaller, more rural hospitals appear to receive slower care, and night-shift and agency staff are the least often heard. Sampling includes night and agency staff at every site, and findings for night care and for the smallest site are reported separately.
effectiveness: The study tells the network what to target; its value is judged by whether the determinants found lead to a specific strategy.
efficiency: Uses network nurse time and existing figures; no new data systems.
costs: Research nurse time released by the network and interview recorders; no other costs.
grants: None needed for this study; the determinants will support an application to fund a strategy trial.
partnerships: The five sepsis leads, the regional sepsis network, and two sepsis survivors or family members from the network's patient panel advising on the interview guide.
rebPath: Research ethics review for staff interviews and observation at five hospitals, with site permissions at each hospital; neither has been requested, so both gates are unknown.
limitations: Staff accounts may not match practice; five sites in one network; no patient interviews.
summary: Low-risk staff study with written consent, protection of identifiable roles, and night and small-site equity reporting; ethics and site gates unknown.
